first_reader_check.about: Whether a published tag on a released mathematics item (a standard code, or a TIMSS cognitive domain) is required to match the key, tested by programs that lack the tagged operation, with no student data.
first_reader_check.shown: Item-writing rules yield no family-wise discovery; one rule beats chance on one cell (EQAO grade 6) and awaits replication. Claims are made only on items whose PDF text layer matches the printed page, and two rows that cleared on the text layer (Algebra II masked-stem, geometry lower-central) fail on those items. Language models of two families recover New York Regents Algebra I keys with the given quantities withheld, on items tagged for recognizing or interpreting a form; on those items a pass does not require the given quantities. TIMSS knowing, applying, and reasoning cells stay null at about 50 to 80 public items each.
first_reader_check.what_is_new: A one-sided program witness on tagged public mathematics, hashed before scoring and Holm-corrected inside three families, whose claims survive a mechanical check of the text layer against the printed page; and the finding that the withheld-quantity language-model result sits on recognition-tagged items and not on execution-tagged ones.
first_reader_check.why_a_big_deal: Accountability and research read a tagged pass as evidence of the tagged competency. Where a program without the operation, or without the given quantities, matches the key, that reading is of the wrong quantity. Half of the released text layer is not what students saw, so any census of released items that does not check the print is measuring a proxy.
